name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: Early US flu season; severity still low
summary: US flu admissions reached 9,584 in the week to 7 Nov, early for the season; seven states at high activity
state: CDC reported 9,584 flu hospital admissions in the week to 7 Nov, with activity higher than usual for the time of year, H1N1 making up 98.9% of subtyped flu A and severity still rated low (CDC). High flu activity was reported in seven states, up from two the week before (AP via KPTV, 14 Nov). Searches on 17 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so an unusually early US season keeps Watch.
for_you: Flu vaccination is the main protection. In the UK, check NHS guidance on eligibility for the free flu vaccine; in the US, follow CDC advice. People with symptoms can reduce spread by staying home where possible.
rubric_hit: Watch: US flu season unusually early (CDC: activity higher than typical for early Nov); no variant of concern

sources.title: Weekly US Influenza Surveillance Report: week 44, ending 7 November 2026
Flu season is off to a very early start. Here's where cases are surging right now

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
